knowledgePattern: Use the pentagon angle sum and an AP midpoint to test an implication and its converse
solution:
The five interior angles total 540∘. The original implication is false: a convex pentagon can have angles 90∘,90∘,90∘,108∘,162∘, which contain 108° but cannot form an arithmetic progression in any order. To construct it, cut off one corner of a rectangle with a straight line making 18° with one edge: the three untouched corners are right angles, and the two new interior angles are 108° and 162°.

A statement and its contrapositive are equivalent, so II is false as well.

For the converse, five angles in an arithmetic progression can be written a−2d,a−d,a,a+d,a+2d. Their sum is 5a=540∘, so the middle one is 108°. Thus III is true. Answer D.

hints.title: Separate the logical statements
hints.body: Write the original and converse as two different arrows. Recall how the contrapositive relates to the original.
hints.recap: A contrapositive reverses and negates both sides; it is equivalent to the original implication.
hints.pitfall: A converse is not automatically equivalent to the original.
hints.pause: Decide which implications require their own proof or counterexample.

hints.title: Use the total and the middle term
hints.body: Find the total interior angle sum of a pentagon. Then write a five-term arithmetic progression symmetrically about its middle term.
hints.recap: For an odd number of equally spaced terms, the average equals the middle term.
hints.pitfall: Any counterexample must satisfy the angle restrictions of a real pentagon.
hints.pause: Test both arrows using the fixed angle total and an allowed nonuniform example.
